page: Microsoft Azure FX48-12mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration classified under the Compute Optimized FXmdsv2 family, uniquely configured with a constrained core count and an expansive memory footprint. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware allocates 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a massive 260 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and modern cryptographic acceleration.

A central characteristic of this instance is its extreme memory-to-core ratio. The server provides 1008.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 84.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast scratch and caching disk performance alongside Azure Premium Storage capability. The instance does not include discrete GPUs (0.0 count) and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show high single-thread capabilities attributable to the 4.2 GHz clock rate and large cache. Geekbench single-core testing reached 2365.0 points, ranking in the top tier, while text processing benchmarks also scored in the top tier at 2927.0. Single-threaded gzip compression scored strongly at 34.55 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression yielded 14.47 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput reflects the physical 6-core limit, with stress-ng multi-core (13318.5) and Geekbench multi-core (11420.0) performing within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 102.55 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 73.18 GB/sec for write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX48-12mds_v2 is optimized for software architectures licensed on a per-core basis that demand massive RAM and high single-thread clock speeds. By constraining the core count to 12 vCPUs while retaining over 1 TB of RAM and high clock frequency, it reduces software license overhead while avoiding memory starvation. This profile makes it suited for large-footprint in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases with high per-core licensing expenses, and high-memory computational modeling.
description: Microsoft Azure FX48-12mds_v2 is a compute and memory-focused virtual machine engineered for high-frequency workloads requiring substantial memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX instruction extensions. It is equipped with 1008.0 GB of system memory (84.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 2832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance alongside average multi-core metrics consistent with its reduced core count. The constrained core allocation paired with large RAM offers license-cost optimization for memory-intensive enterprise software, large in-memory databases, and high-frequency analytical processing.
